item.title: Mariners make major decision on future of franchise
item.description: The MLB offseason is already bringing significant changes to the Seattle Mariners, who have reportedly made a major decision regarding the future of their organization by hiring Jason Kanzler as the team’s new manager. Reports emerged Tuesday indicating that Seattle has selected the 36-year-old to lead the franchise moving forward. Although the Mariners have not officially announced the hiring, an announcement is expected later Tuesday. Source confirms to @Chandler_Rome: Jason Kanzler is the Mariners’ new manager. First: @DKramer_ — Ken Rosenthal (@Ken_Rosenthal) November 3, 2026 Kanzler was one of two finalists for the position, with former Houston Astros manager Joe Espada also in consideration. The decision represents a significant opportunity for Kanzler, who will take on his first managerial role at any level of professional baseball. MORE: Yankees moving on from All-Star after 2.5 seasons Kanzler gets first opportunity as MLB manager Feb 23, 2023; West Palm Beach, FL, USA; Houston Astros major league coach Jason Kanzler (41) poses for a portrait during photo day at The Ballpark of the Palm Beaches. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-USA TODAY Sports Kanzler brings experience in player development, having spent the past three seasons with the Chicago Cubs as the organization’s director of player development. His background working with young talent and helping players progress through an organization appears to have made him an appealing candidate for Seattle as the franchise looks toward the future. At just 36 years old, Kanzler will become the 22nd manager in Mariners franchise history. He will also be among the youngest managers in Major League Baseball. In fact, Kanzler will become the second-youngest manager in the Majors, trailing only Washington Nationals manager Blake Butera, who is 34 years old. While this will be his first opportunity to manage a professional baseball team, Kanzler will now face the challenge of leading a major-league organization with expectations of competing at the highest level. item.title: J.J. Spaun Recalls Cleaning Harris English’s Shoes
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The 2025 U.S. Open champion once cleaned the shoes of the player who beat him in a crucial amateur final. J.J. Spaun worked the locker room at Torrey Pines while a student, scrubbing the mud off the white shoes of Harris English. English had defeated Spaun in the quarterfinals of the 2011 U.S. Amateur Public Links just months before. The irony of the situation remains a favorite story for Spaun, who now holds a major trophy while English has five PGA Tour wins. The job was a fundraiser for the San Diego State men’s golf team. Spaun walked on without a scholarship in 2009 before earning a partial one. The team program worked the Farmers Insurance Open every year to raise cash for their program. Spaun recalled the moment English walked into the shoe room on a rainy day. The pro arrived with white shoes covered in mud and simply said, “JJ.” Spaun replied, according to Yardbarker , “Yeah, man. Here, I’ll take your shoes. Give me your shoes.” The Money That Never Reached the Worker English tipped well for the service, but the cash never reached Spaun’s pocket. The team rules required all tip money to go directly to the school program. Spaun noted the frustration of the long drive to the course without extra cash. “Yes, Harris took care of us, but we didn’t get to count the tips. I was like, ‘Come on, man. I need some gas. It’s a 30-minute drive each way.’ But apparently, the money went to the program,” Spaun said. He added that modern NIL rules might have allowed players to keep that cash today. The match that started this dynamic happened in June 2011 at Bandon Dunes. At age 20, Spaun competed against English, a Georgia alum and Walker Cup contender who had recently graduated. The winner of that event earned a Masters invitation, raising the stakes high. On the par-five 17th hole, Spaun fell behind by one stroke just as his performance deteriorated. A two-stroke penalty was levied because he marked his ball away from the green. The eagle putt turned into a par attempt, causing him to forfeit both the hole and the match. From the Shoe Room to the Winner’s Circle English reached the semifinals of that 2011 event before Corbin Mills won the title. English secured his 2012 PGA Tour card by finishing in a tie for 13th place at the 2011 Q-School. Shortly thereafter, he entered the Torrey Pines shoe room as a professional who received payment. Spaun described the feeling of shining shoes for men he had recently beaten in competition. “By the time you’re a senior, you’re like, there’s all these freakin* guys that like I was just beaten up on like last year that are on tour now, and I’m shining the freakin* shoes. So, yeah, it kind of like wore off, you know, the beauty of it,” Spaun said. Both men have moved far past those early days on the tour. item.title: Steven Alker says some PGA Tour Champions golfers don't want LIV golfers
item.description: PHOENIX — The PGA Tour Champions has reached its season finale at the Charles Schwab Cup Championship . After two playoff events, there's a week off before the postseason finale. There are 36 golfers who qualify for the tournament each year and while Champions stalwart Bernhard Langer is not here for the first time in his senior tour career (since 2008), the field has most of the rest of the big names on the circuit. But could the Champions tour look dramatically different in 2027 and beyond after a number of LIV defections? What about the prospect of Tiger Woods finally taking up senior golf? More: Inside Tiger Woods’ potential comeback: What Golfweek has learned about his return Steven Alker, a two-time winner of the season-long points race, was asked at a media day on Monday, Nov. 2, at Phoenix Country Club about those prospects. "It's a Catch-22," Alker said of players 50 and older leaving LIV and being granted access to the PGA Tour Champions. "We want players to keep the profile of the tour up. And then you got guys on the tour who don't want those guys at all. "I'm not gonna name names, but that has been talked about on the PAC board and that's an ongoing thing. Where do you draw the line? Who you should be penalized more than some other guy, you know? I think that's going on right now. Some guys have gotten six months, some guys got a year [suspension]. Do we change the rules for those guys coming out? There's a lot of talk going on right now. ... but that's up to the player directors and our president, you know, for where that goes. But I can tell you there are talks going on. And I know it's very split." "You know, yes, we should try and keep the profile to keep the tour going. I'm all for that, but then on the flip side, who do we let in? What's the time frame here? What are we working on, you know? So it's tough." What about Tiger Woods playing PGA Tour Champions? Woods and Bobby Jones each have nine U.S. Golf Association titles and the general assumption has been that Woods is eyeing a U.S. Senior Open trophy to break the tie. But what about a somewhat regular senior schedule for Tiger? "This talk, yeah, he seriously wants to come out, there's inside talking," Alker said. "He wants to come out and play, and in particular, I think the big events, like the invitationals or Stricker's event and the Furyk event. He's got his buddies who really him to do their events. You got the USGA, you got the U.S Senior Open. He wants to add to his tally, you know? "I seriously think he'll come out if he gets fit and in the right mind." item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. item.title: Lucas Herbert Reveals Major Contention Sparked LIV Exit
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images As the league moves to finalize its 2027 roster under pressure, Lucas Herbert has become the first Australian to confirm his departure from LIV Golf. The move comes after Herbert realized that competing in majors was his true priority, a goal that the rebel league could not support under its current structure. While Cameron Smith and other high-profile Aussies remain in limbo, Herbert has already made his choice clear. He is set to return to the PGA Tour of Australasia next week for the NSW Open. Herbert spoke on the Tee It Up podcast to explain his reasoning, stating he has “no regrets” about joining the Saudi-backed circuit initially. He acknowledged the value of his time there, noting the friendships formed with peers like Cam Smith, Marc Leishman, and Matt Jones. “I feel I have been incredibly lucky to get the opportunities I have. To spend so much time around Cam and Leish, Jonesy (Matt Jones) and Elvis, as well,” he said during the interview reported by Fox Sports. He added that the environment allowed him to learn and grow, describing it as a “really cool environment that we had, for the best part of three years.” The Major Contention Epiphany The turning point for Herbert occurred during his performance at The Open Championship. According to Fox Sports , the experience of leading a major tournament sparked a realization that conflicted with the LIV model. Herbert recalled the week he spent in contention at The Open, calling it “incredible.” This feeling of being on the biggest stage made him question if the limited schedule of the rebel league was sufficient for his career goals. He emphasized that financial gain was not the driving factor behind his exit. “I’m not super caught up in how much money I play for … but genuinely for me I want to see my game improve, I want to give myself the best chance to play in majors, to compete in majors,” Herbert told the podcast. The desire to compete in the four majors every year proved incompatible with the LIV contract, which required players to wear team uniforms and limited their ability to enter traditional tour events without facing bans. Schedule Limitations and Future Paths Herbert highlighted the structural issues within LIV Golf’s planned schedule for the upcoming season as a primary reason for his exit. The league reportedly told players the season would consist of only ten tournaments, with vague promises of additional “extra playing opportunities.” Herbert found this insufficient for a professional career. He was blunt about the math, stating, “For me 10 events is not enough to build a season around.” This lack of competitive volume forced him to look elsewhere. The PGA Tour of Australasia offers a more traditional schedule, and Herbert is ready to resume play there. item.title: DAZN secures option for global streaming rights to 2029 Club World Cup
item.description: Credit: Hannah Mckay-Reuters via Imagn Images DAZN, the London-based sports streaming service that proved to be FIFA’s saving grace during the inaugural 32-team Club World Cup in 2025, appears to be in pole position to broadcast the event again in 2029. According to a report by Matt Hughes in The Guardian , DAZN has secured “an exclusive option” to be the exclusive global streamer for the 2029 competition, which is expected to expand from 32 clubs to 48. When DAZN would need to decide on its option is unknown. Financial details of the deal were also unreported. DAZN somewhat infamously saved FIFA from embarrassment ahead of the 2025 Club World Cup after FIFA failed to secure a deal with Apple TV. Reports from the time suggest that Apple expressed serious interest in the property , but balked at FIFA’s high asking price. DAZN met FIFA’s astronomical $1 billion ask, but seemingly as a sort of quid pro quo that involved Saudi investment in the company that more or less translated into FIFA awarding the 2034 World Cup to Saudi Arabia. Shortly before DAZN’s surprising last-minute bid for the Club World Cup, a Saudi Arabian investment group, Surj Sports Investment, purchased a 10% stake in DAZN. Capital from that sale was then used to fund the $1 billion purchase of Club World Cup rights. At practically the very same time, FIFA announced Saudi Arabia would host the 2034 World Cup. Considering the 2025 rights purchase amounted to essentially a thinly veiled bribe, the actual value of Club World Cup rights are anyone’s guess. DAZN’s deal is streaming-focused, leaving the door open for linear partners to join the streamer in domestic markets. In 2025, TNT Sports partnered with DAZN to air select Club World Cup matches on cable. Plans for the 2029 Club World Cup are far from finalized, with FIFA still working to firm up a format and location for the tournament. It is believed the event will take place in Morocco, or perhaps shared between Morocco and Spain, should FIFA president Gianni Infantino survive reelection in March amid fallout from his scrapped proposal to sell equity stakes in the World Cup to private entities. Morocco and Spain are two of the three primary host countries for the 2030 World Cup, and The Guardian cites Infantino’s cozy relationship with King Mohammed VI of Morocco as reason the Club World Cup would likely land there if the FIFA president is reelected. The competition would also serve as a test run of sorts, similar to how the 2025 Club World Cup gave the United States a dry run ahead of 2026. item.title: Packers QB Jordan Love leads NFL in passing yards, on pace for team record
item.description: Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love leads the NFL in passing yards and is on pace to set the team's franchise record for single season passing yards through eight weeks of the 2026 season. Love has 2,246 passing yards, placing him 100 yards clear of Matthew Stafford for the NFL lead. He is one of only five quarterbacks with at least 2,000 passing yards after eight weeks. Love is averaging 280.8 passing yards per game, which would put him on pace for 4,772 passing yards over 17 games. Aaron Rodgers holds the franchise record for passing yards in a season with 4,643, which he accomplished over only 15 games during his spectacular 2011 season. Love's 280.8-yard average would rank third in franchise history. Love leads the NFL in passing attempts at 312. At his current pace of 39 attempts per game, Love would shatter the previous franchise record of 613, set by Brett Favre in 2006. Love is on pace for 663; only three times has a Packers quarterback attempted at least 600 passes in a season (Favre, 2006; Rodgers, 2016; Favre 2005). Without a run game, the Packers have become ever more reliant on Love and his ability to move the ball through the air. There have been no signs of improvement in the run game, even with veteran offensive line additions and the return of Josh Jacobs, suggesting Love will need to continue carrying the offense with his right arm. Overall, Love is on pace for 4,772 passing yards, 34 passing touchdowns and 12 interceptions. There have been only nine seasons by a quarterback in team history with at least 4,000 passing yards, 30 passing touchdowns and fewer than 15 interceptions in a season -- Rodgers has seven, Favre has one and Love has one (2023). item.title: ‘I didn’t realise…’ – Caitlin Clark explains viral moment where she refused to wear Colts jersey
item.description: Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images Caitlin Clark has revealed what went down when she was given an Indianapolis Colts jersey when the Indiana Fever star and her teammates visited the Lucas Oil Stadium last season. The three-time WNBA All-Star was gifted a Colts jersey with her name and jersey number 22 printed on it. Her teammates also got their own jerseys and were waving to the crowd, who were applauding them. What caught the attention of fans was the fact that Clark was the only Fever player who did not wear the Colts jersey and had it in her hand while acknowledging the appreciation from everyone in the stadium. The real reason why Clark did not wear the Colts jersey is that she is a fan of the Kansas City Chiefs. “Honestly, in real time I wasn’t thinking, ‘I’m not going to put this on’; I don’t want the Chiefs fans mad or Travis mad, but after the fact I didn’t realise all my teammates had it on. So that made it look a bit worse, but whatever. I still have the jersey, it’s cool, they put my name on it,” said Clark on the Not gonna lie with Kylie Kelce. The 24-year-old has been a longtime Chiefs fan, and there are pictures of her wearing the team’s jersey when she was just a child. Recently, she was even spotted at Arrowhead as the Chiefs played the Los Angeles Chargers, sitting alongside Taylor Swift. While she is a big Chiefs fan, Clark stated that she also had to show her loyalty to Indiana, as she plays for a sports team in the state. “I usually try to make it to like one Colts game a year. I have to support, obviously, the hometown team, but it’s not the same level of fandom,” Clark added. As one of the biggest sports stars to play in Indiana, Clark understands how much she means to the state. She has also made appearances during Indiana Pacers games to support her friend Tyrese Haliburton. With the WNBA season having come to an end and the NFL season having reached midway, Clark might soon be at the Lucas Oil Stadium to watch a Colts game. item.title: Joel Embiid admits he's struggling to adjust to new role with 76ers: 'I need to touch the ball'
item.description: Joel Embiid admits he's struggling to adjust to new role with 76ers: 'I need to touch the ball' originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Joel Embiid is dealing with more than playing with a right foot plantar fascia injury. The 2023 MVP is adjusting to no longer being the focal point on the 76ers ’ offense. “For me, it’s a little bit of an adjustment,” Embiid said following Monday’s 127-106 victory over the Chicago Bulls at Xfinity Mobile Arena. “I’m such a rhythm guy,” he added. “And over the years, obviously, I’ve had a lot of opportunities to just touch the ball almost every other possession. And [now] sometimes you can just go four or five possessions in a row where you don’t touch the ball. So that’s where it’s kind of like an adjustment where I’m not used to catch-and-shoot as much.” The 7-foot-2 center is used to creating for himself and others. “So I’m working on that,” he said of the adjustments. Embiid came into this season with a career average of 27.6 points while attempting 18.2 shots per game. The 11th-year veteran attempted 9.9 free throws and led the league in scoring during the 2021-22 and 2022-23 seasons. Through seven games this season, Embiid is averaging career lows of 18.5 points and 6.7 free throw attempts. His 15.2 shot attempts are the second lowest of his career. The seven-time All-Star’s decreased usage rate is part of the sacrifices that come with the offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, both former NBA Finals MVPs. On most nights, he’s been the third option behind Tyrese Maxey (20.4 shots per game) and Brown (16.6). However, James (13.7) and VJ Edgecombe (11.3) aren’t far behind Embiid in shot attempts. “My mindset is really on whenever I have the ball: make plays,” Embiid said. “Make the game easy for all these guys. Making the right play over and over, setting screens, getTyrese as open as possible, Bron, all these guys. … That’s really been what the focus is on. “And then, on the other side also, working on myself. How can I get back to the level of dominance, but without having as [many] touches as I’m used to?” In addition to fewer shot attempts, Embiid is shooting career lows from the field (.407) and on three-pointers (.130). He should get more opportunities to raise his level of domination when healthier. Because of a minutes restriction, Embiid sat out the fourth quarter of Monday’s victory. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander brought 'better personal energy' in OKC's win over Cavaliers
item.description: Visibly annoyed at Mario Hezonja's handsy defense, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's body language had enough. He pulled his dribble back to the perimeter. Dancing with the ball in a crossover, he went the disrespectful route of going with the pull-up outside jumper he drilled in his. The moxie move was certainly different from his somber Saturday mood. The Oklahoma City Thunder collected a much-needed 117-112 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers . It's a quick morale boost as the former continues to navigate life in the Post-D.C.C. (Dub, Chet, Caso) era. Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 43 points on 14-of-35 shooting, eight assists and three rebounds. He shot 4-of-8 from 3 and went 11-of-12 on free throws. He also had two steals and one block. This is what the Thunder need. At least, for the interim. As ruthless as OKC's recent circumstances are, you can't reasonably pack your bags and call it a year with 75-plus games to go. Gilgeous-Alexander finally understands the mission. He has to leave it all on the floor. Every single night. It's not a sustainable formula for success, but a quick fix that they need for now. The super-efficient 30-point scorer went against his nature. Usually, he plays within the flow of the offense. That's no longer a luxury. Almost all of OKC's possessions with him on the floor have to end with him taking a shot attempt. That's what happened throughout the night. Chet Holmgren and Jalen Williams encouraged him from a distance. item.title: Real Madrid loanee earns Argentina call-up after impressive Serie A performance
item.description: Real Madrid loanee earns Argentina call-up after impressive Serie A performance Real Madrid loaned out Franco Mastantuono to Fiorentina back in the summer in the hope that he would get regular game time and adapt to European football. The 19-year-old South American starlet had a difficult first season in the Spanish capital despite starting brightly. Mastantuono took some time to get going at Fiorentina, but his performances have steadily improved of late. Fresh off the back of a goalscoring display against Sassuolo, Mastantuono has now earned recognition at international level. Lionel Scaloni has included the 19-year-old in Argentina’s squad for the November international break. The World Cup runners-up have friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica scheduled for November 13 and 17. Mastantuono’s involvement in Scaloni’s team follows his return to the international set-up back in September. Mastantuono rewarded for impressive Fiorentina form Against Sassuolo last night , Mastantuono scored once and contributed significantly in possession, completing three dribbles, winning six duels and registering six ball recoveries. His latest goal also took his Serie A tally to four in his first 10 appearances, an impressive return for a teenager adjusting to Italian football. He became the second-youngest player to score four Serie A goals in his first 10 appearances. The youngster has shown much more confidence in recent games, and his overall influence on attacking play has increased. These are the kind of developments Real Madrid would have hoped for when they sent him out on loan, and things seem to be working out so far. Argentina recognition strengthens Madrid’s long-term hopes Mastantuono was unlikely to get many first-team minutes had he chosen to stay at Real Madrid this season. Jose Mourinho has enough attacking options at his disposal, and at 19, what the Argentine attacker needed was regular game time. Mastantuono is developing well on his loan spell. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) His performances have now given Scaloni another reason to keep him involved as the national team prepares for life after Lionel Messi. Competition for places in the national team is immense, especially with someone like Nico Paz ahead of him, and Mastantuono needs to prove that he deserves minutes under Scaloni. There is still no clarity on what the future holds for Mastantuono in the Spanish capital and whether Mourinho sees him as part of his team in the upcoming seasons. If not, a good loan spell could help drum up interest in the teenager from other European clubs and earn Real Madrid a good transfer fee. It remains to be seen whether Mastantuono gets a chance with Argentina and how he fares over the course of the season.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Moorhead’s top-ranked Class 6A football team may have to chase a state championship without one of the state’s best players. Senior wide receiver David Mack suffered a potentially season-ending injury in the Spuds’ 64-29 first-round playoff win over Coon Rapids on Friday, according to the Star Tribune. The severity of the injury has not been disclosed. Mack left the game in the first half with an apparent upper-body injury and did not return. The Star Tribune reported that he stayed in the game for a time before asking to be taken out. Minnesota High School Football Section Tournament Championship Matchups Before leaving, Mack helped his teammate make history. He caught the 23-yard touchdown pass from senior quarterback Jett Feeney that broke Joe Mauer’s top classification record for touchdown passes in a season, then added a 15-yard score for a 14-0 lead. He finished with five catches for 82 yards and two touchdowns. Mack leads Minnesota with 24 receiving touchdowns this season and has 69 catches for 1,230 yards through nine games, according to the Star Tribune. Last season he set a state record with 121 receptions, adding 1,607 yards and 26 touchdowns as Moorhead reached the Class 6A championship game. The Spuds fell to Edina 42-35 in a record-breaking Prep Bowl. He is the state’s top-rated wide receiver prospect by 247sports.com. Mack committed to the Golden Gophers in March and is one of four Moorhead players in Minnesota’s 2027 recruiting class. He is a three-star prospect and the sixth-best player in Minnesota in the Class of 2027. He is one of eight commits from Minnesota in the Golden Gophers’ 2027 recruiting class. Reich is also a passing option out of the backfield. He has 36 receptions for 297 yards and three touchdowns. Other Spuds will need to step up in Mack’s absence. item.title: Pocognoli focus on Scotland tidy-up as Euros loom
item.description: When Sebastien Pocognoli's disjointed Scotland trudged off at a two-thirds-full Hampden after being well beaten by Slovenia, the intrigue that came with the start of the new boss' extended maiden camp had turned to a sense of deflation. A dominant display in a Nations League draw away to the Slovenians 10 days prior, plus another in a 2-0 victory at North Macedonia, had built optimism. A 3-0 defeat at home to Switzerland was written off after Jack Hendry's early red card was quickly followed by an opening goal for the 12th-ranked Fifa nation. A second straight Hampden loss under the Belgian felt different, though. Pocognoli's side were "outfought" and simply "not good enough", said captain Andy Robertson. Cut open defensively throughout by Slovenia, placed nine spots below Scotland in the world rankings, a sobering second-half showing led to questions about approach, systems and squad make-up. However, heading into a double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland this month, which will conclude the Scots' Nations League campaign, Pocognoli insists this is more of a clean-up job rather than one that requires any radical change. "We want to continue what we produced in the first camp," the 39-year-old said after naming his latest squad , which marks the returns of Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Kieran Tierney, while James Penrice has received a first call-up as reward for an impressive run of form with Rangers. "There's no reason to change everything because I was happy with the camp. The main word is continuity [after the first camp]. "It's important to get some good results for sure. I was clear we need to find the right balance between changing things, experimenting and also being successful." McTominay returns as Penrice earns first Scotland call Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony Pocognoli seeks mood-shifting result In football's savage, reactive world, a deserved defeat at home to a team ranked outside the world's top 50 is bound to attract scrutiny. Given it was the final match of a four-game run before a six-week wait to attempt to put things right, that criticism only becomes prolonged. Pocognoli shared the Tartan Army's disappointment, but after a few days the "real feeling" came after a debut camp packed with new faces and "strong decisions". "When the disappointment was gone, the first feeling was positive," he said. "We did a lot of good things. "But we need a good result to give something to the supporters and give confidence to the players that we are winning games - that's the main factor in qualifying for tournaments. "We want to just continue the good things we showed in Slovenia and North Macedonia in a very short period of time, to keep the fragment of these games and to try to clean some situations." item.title: What Zac Taylor said about facing former Bengals DB Jessie Bates III
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor shared praise of Atlanta Falcons defensive back Jessie Bates III ahead of an NFL Week 9 meeting in Madrid, Spain. The Bengals' second-round pick in the 2018 NFL Draft is set to face his former team for the first time since leaving Cincinnati for Atlanta after the 2022 season. "I feel like I've just seen him a lot on TV, on tape, and I think we all love Jessie," Taylor told reporters Nov. 2 . "Everybody feels the same way about Jessie here. And (I've) always been pulling for him and really happy to see him be successful, a Pro Bowler (in 2023), like he's earned all that and (is a) really easy guy to root for. So when we play him, we've played a lot of people I know and like, and it's not going to change anything when you get on the field. But (I) have been very happy to see Jessie out there having success." Taylor was asked what it was like to coach Bates for four seasons. "Well, he was a very young player when I got here," Taylor said. "He was what in his second year in my first year? So, new scheme comes in and so he's got to adjust to that. So just like any player he's growing, you know, and had his difficult moments (and) had his really good moments. And I think in really in years three, four, five is where Jessie really took off and was really playing at an unbelievable level." "And you could just see his confidence increase every single year to where his playmaking abilities really just took over," Taylor continued. "Plays on the ball. Interceptions. His tackling got better and better every single year to become a really good tackler, really good communicator. He was really just a perfect example of a guy that just shows growth from every year from years one through five and (it's) probably the way he attacked it (with a) professional mindset." "Great guy in the community," Taylor added. "Great guy in the locker room. Easy to coach because he likes being coached, likes ball and I don't usually spend this time much praising the other team, but Jessie's one that I've always really liked." Bates played in 79 games over five seasons with the Bengals. He has played in 59 games over four seasons in Atlanta. Bates has one interception through eight games this season. He's returned an interception for a touchdown in each of the past three seasons. item.title: Andoni Iraola gives Ryan Gravenberch injury update after Liverpool star misses Fenerbahce trip
item.description: Andoni Iraola has not ruled out a possible return for Ryan Gravenberch this weekend after it was confirmed the Dutchman will play no part in the club’s Champions League trip to Fenerbahce through injury. Liverpool midfielder Gravenberch was absent from the 22-man travelling squad that flew out to Turkey on Tuesday morning, left behind on Merseyside to have treatment on a heel issue. Iraola provided an update on the 24-year-old’s status at a press conference at Fenerbahce’s Chobani Stadium, which was delayed by over an hour due to traffic issues in Istanbul. Asked if Gravenberch could be available again for this Sunday’s trip to Crystal Palace, he said: “I don’t know, it’s a day-to-day thing. It’s the heel, it’s about the pain. Ryan Gravenberch is sidelined for Liverpool's trip to Fenerbahce with a heel problem (Getty) “I think he’s been in some discomfort. The other day against Arsenal, he was warming up and he was not fully confident. He hasn't improved since then, but it's going be something that every day we ask him, every day we see how he is. “If he can be available for the weekend, lovely. It would be a very good help for us, but I cannot tell you right now.” The Netherlands international was an unused substitute in Sunday’s defeat to Arsenal , with Trey Nyoni preferred in midfield as the 19-year-old made his first Premier League start. Gravenberch’s absence likely opens up another opportunity for Nyoni in the starting XI against Fenerbahce. Trey Nyoni made his first Premier League start on the weekend after being preferred to Gravenberch (Getty) “ I think he has to continue in the same place that has been since the beginning of pre-season, being ready for every game,” Iraola added. “I think he's playing most of the games or even all the games lately, so we trust him. “He's doing very well and I think we have to encourage him to continue improving, continue learning, continue adding experience. But he's in a very good place.” Iraola was left furious after the Arsenal result after a penalty appeal surrounding a shirt-pull on Alexander Isak was waved away by referee Andy Madley and VAR, asserting after the game that he will tell his players to dive in order to get officials to take appropriate action. Despite his anger, Iraola confirmed that he had not asked refereeing body Pro Ref for a formal explanation why the penalty wasn’t awarded. “No, I didn’t ask for an explanation,” he said. “I told you what I think about the plays, but honestly I don’t have time. “Preparing for Fenerbahce, we have just two days between games, so I’ve just been focussing on this game, the opposition and how to prepare the team for tomorrow.”

item.title: Share a Card With an NHL Star: Inside Upper Deck’s New “2 of a Kind” Program
item.description: Card manufacturers are increasingly searching for ways to add true utility to sports cards. In today’s hobby, utility means pulling more than just a rare piece of cardboard—it means unlocking player visits, VIP experiences, additional memorabilia, or exclusive 1-of-1 bounties. We have seen this play out recently with “Follow Back” cards, where redeeming the hit guarantees the featured athlete follows the collector on Instagram. Topps has also leaned heavily into utility, randomly inserting tickets to the Home Run Derby and All-Star events directly into packs. One of the highest-profile examples occurred in 2023, when Topps invited anyone who pulled a green /99 Victor Wembanyama autograph from 2022-23 Bowman Chrome U to a private event with the rising star, culminating in one collector receiving Wemby’s special “My first auto card.” On the ultra-high-end side of the market, Topps operates the Three Kings platform , a bounty program where collectors who assemble a player’s three rarest cards unlock a special exclusive issue. Recently, manufacturers have started experimenting with shared player-collector print runs. To celebrate the Milwaukee Brewers’ 2026 World Series victory, every player in the Topps NOW championship team set , which must be purchased by November 4, has a Diamond Parallel limited to just two copies: one gifted to the player inside a custom diamond chain, and the matching copy randomly inserted into a collector’s set. Now, Upper Deck is taking this shared collector-athlete utility to the next level with the announcement of its new “ 2 of a Kind ” program. Debuting in the 2026-27 O-Pee-Chee release, the program features an extensive 100-player NHL checklist designed to forge a direct connection between the fan and the athlete. The premise is straightforward: the cards are printed as a matching set of exactly two. The 1-of-2 card is gifted directly to the featured NHL player, while the 2-of-2 card is inserted into packs for the public. The cards will stand out aesthetically, featuring a metallic foilboard front and a rose gold substrate on the back. Upper Deck’s Director of Sports Brands, Paul Zickler, emphasized the accessibility of the chase, noting that these matching pairs will debut in an approachable product available at both hobby shops and major retailers. Crucially, Zickler confirmed that the cards are live in packs, meaning collectors will not have to deal with redemptions. “The feeling of pulling a rare card of your favorite player is unique, and it’s hard to recreate. That, plus our constant goal of trying to connect collectors with their favorite players, was the basis for 2 of a Kind,” said Jason Masherah, President of Upper Deck. “With only two cards being created of each player, them getting one and a collector getting the other, we can’t wait to see the reactions and interactions this program brings for years to come.” The utility of the 2-of-2 card extends beyond simply sharing a print run with an NHL star. item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images As LIV Golf tries a major reboot, Bryson DeChambeau has signaled most strongly that he intends to return to the circuit. The two-time U.S. Open champion appeared on the “Figuring Out” podcast to discuss the league’s future following its Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing in September. While other stars have walked away, DeChambeau believes the new financial structure will finally work for the players and the organization. According to Central Oregon Daily , DeChambeau told host Raj Shamani that the league can now “make full financial sense.” He emphasized that the new model is being built to survive the long term. “The business model makes a lot of sense,” DeChambeau told host Raj Shamani. He added that the upcoming version of the tour will be handled correctly. “It’s no funny business, no nothing. It’s going to be done right. And this is going to be a league, hopefully, that exists forever.” Bankruptcy and Player Exodus The comments were made amid severe financial trouble. Money problems forced the league to end its 2026 season early, leading it to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September. This financial collapse triggered a wave of departures. Tim Schmitt reported for Central Oregon Daily that at least 14 notable players have said they will not return to the new league. Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, and Sergio Garcia are among those who have opted out. Instead of joining LIV, Sergio Garcia, the 2017 Masters champion, plans to compete on the DP World Tour in 2027. Richard Bland, Cameron Tringale, Brendan Steele, Victor Perez, and Ben Campbell have publicly declared their commitment. item.title: Baltimore Ravens sign veteran quarterback after Lamar Jackson injury
item.description: Charles LeClaire-USA TODAY Sports The Baltimore Ravens’ quarterback room has been decimated by injuries over the past few days. Now, the team is bringing in some reinforcements. The Ravens are signing quarterback Kedon Slovis to their 53-man roster off the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad. He could be one of Baltimore’s options against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. Ravens’ Quarterback Injuries Lamar Jackson suffered a right thumb injury on his first throw of Sunday’s 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He’s set to undergo surgery and is headed to injured reserve, and head coach Jesse Minter said the injury could “potentially” end his season. Backup Tyler Huntley then went down with a toe injury in the second quarter, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Fagnano went 10-of-21 for 91 yards with an interception. Fagnano is now dealing with an ankle injury of his own and was limited at Monday’s walkthrough, though Minter said he expects him “to have a chance to play on Thursday.” The Ravens also signed Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday. Baltimore, which dropped to 4-4 with the loss, has reportedly shown interest in trading for a veteran quarterback as well. Kedon Slovis Joins the Ravens On Tuesday, the Ravens added another option at the position, signing Slovis off the Green Bay Packers practice squad. “A new QB in Baltimore: The Ravens are signing Kedon Slovis to their 53-man roster off the Packers’ practice squad, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports. The options for Thursday night against Jacksonville now include Joe Fagnano, Austin Reed and Slovis,” wrote Tom Pelissero . Slovis, 25, played college football at USC, Pitt, and BYU before making his NFL debut with the Arizona Cardinals last season. He appeared in two games and attempted just two passes. Ironically, his debut came against the Jaguars, when he replaced Jacoby Brissett after Brissett took a big hit from linebacker Devin Lloyd. He also has a connection to Baltimore’s coaching staff. Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork was Slovis’ position coach in Arizona last season. “Ravens QB coach Israel Woolfork was with Kedon Slovis in Arizona. Now, they’re back together in Baltimore,” Pelissero added . Needless to say, it’s been a chaotic week for the Ravens at quarterback, and it’s only Tuesday. item.title: Lucas Herbert Reveals The Real Reason LIV Golfers Are Leaving
item.description: Dennis Schneidler-Imagn Images Lucas Herbert has admitted that money is not the reason he is walking away from LIV Golf, even though he earned over $25 million during his three seasons there. The Australian golfer says the brutal travel demands and a shrinking schedule are what pushed him toward the DP World Tour. He told a podcast that he wants to see his game improve and get better chances to play in majors. Herbert finished fourth on the LIV season-long standings in 2026 after winning two events. Despite the big paycheck, he is joining the ranks of players like Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia who are returning to the traditional tours. The move comes as LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September and secured new funding that depends on keeping a “critical mass” of players. The Travel Toll That Money Cannot Fix Many fans assume players leave LIV because the prize money is lower or the prestige is gone. Herbert says the schedule is the real problem. He explained that the distance between venues has become too much for anyone to handle. The Australian pointed out that the old schedule with 14 events was easier when many were in America. Now, players fly from the US to Korea, then to Spain, and back to the US, all while trying to get ready for the US Open the following week. “That’s a really tough schedule,” Herbert noted, according to Yahoo Sports . He added that if the DP World Tour had a route like that, no one would play it because it is just too big of a travel grind. The constant jet lag from playing in such huge gaps between venues became the breaking point for many. In 2024, Herbert became a member of Cameron Smith’s Ripper GC upon joining LIV Golf. But the new version of the league, LIV Golf 2.0, plans to have only 10 tournaments. Herbert sees a problem with that number. “Ten events is not enough to build a season around,” he said, according to Yahoo Sports . He worries that adding more events would just lower the quality of the fields and venues. Understanding The Tension On Tour Herbert knows that some DP World Tour members are unhappy about LIV players returning. Many of those players have spent years grinding to keep their spots on the tour. Herbert admits he understands the frustration from both sides. “You know, I’m kind of staying out of those conversations because there are so many moving parts and there are frustrations from both sides too, which I actually, I really understand,” Herbert admitted. He sees the issue of players losing spots or status as a real concern for those who stayed. “Frustration with guys who are potentially losing spots in tournaments or losing status,” he said. Herbert thinks the next year will be strange and interesting until everything sorts itself out. “So, it’s gonna be a really strange and interesting next 12 months until it all kind of sorts itself out again and guys kind of find their feet of where they’re going to play their golf,” he told the Tee It Up Podcast.
